{{Quote|The Force can have a strong influence on the weak-minded.|[[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] to [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]]|audio=MindTrick.flac|<ref name="ANH" />}}
'''Mind tricks''', '''Mind-touch''', or '''mind control''', refer to a spectrum of [[Force power/Legends|Force powers]] which influenced the thoughts of sentient creatures, most commonly used to coerce into agreement by suggestion through '''voice manipulation''', or to cause one to reveal information. This allowed its practitioners to resolve matters in a [[Form Zero/Legends|non-violent way]]. It could also be used to appeal to a sensory impression for distraction or cause friendly fire among enemies.

==Description==
A mind trick was the use of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] to alter a target's perceptions or to plant a suggestion in their mind. It usually worked on the weak-minded.<ref name="Essential Guide to the Force" /> Mind tricks could also be used to implant a false stimulus, such as an image or sound, into an individual's mind for the purpose of distracting them.<ref name="RPG-Core">''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Core Rulebook]]''</ref> There were some species that were particularly resistant to mind tricks, such as [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]], [[Toydarian/Legends|Toydarians]], [[Falleen/Legends|Falleen]], [[Geonosian/Legends|Geonosians]], and [[Dashade/Legends|Dashade]].<ref name="Saga Edition Core Rulebook" />

==Applications==
Examples of mind tricks included persuading another person to do something they would find unpalatable, creating a sensation of fear in a person, or causing them to see or hear things that were not there, including illusions.<ref name="Essential Guide to the Force" />

===Force persuasion===
{{Quote|Your mind powers will not work on me, boy.|[[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]] to Luke Skywalker|translated=1|<ref name="Episode 6">{{Film|VI}}</ref>}}
Force persuasion was the use of the Force to exert influence. Some species with highly organized mental facilities were known to be inherently resistant to its effects, requiring more skill, among them [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]], [[Toydarian/Legends|Toydarians]], [[Yinchorri/Legends|Yinchorri]], [[Kloodavian]]s,<ref name="Episode I Adventures 1: Search for the Lost Jedi">''[[Episode I Adventures 1: Search for the Lost Jedi]]''</ref> [[Dashade/Legends|Dashade]], [[Falleen/Legends|Falleen]], [[Geonosian/Legends|Geonosians]], and possibly [[Snivvian/Legends|Snivvians]]. For example, [[Revan/Legends|Revan]] could persuade [[Motta]] the Hutt, but [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] failed in his attempt to persuade [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba]] the Hutt. Also during the [[Jedi Civil War]], certain ranks of soldiers were trained to resist this technique.<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]'': Revealed if the Jedi Exile attempts to Force persuade the mercenaries who captured Master Vrook.</ref> On the other hand, some species, such as the [[Nikto/Legends|Nikto]], were particularly susceptible to it.<ref name="ANN">''[[The Old Republic: Annihilation]]''</ref> Known variants included affect mind and dominate mind, with dominate mind being a more advanced version of the former.

[[File:Qui-Gon_mind_trick.png|thumb|left|250px|[[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] attempting to use a mind trick on [[Watto/Legends|Watto]]]]
When using a Jedi mind trick, a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] often waved his or her hand to aid in the persuasion. The Jedi adopted a peculiar tone of voice along with a casual facial expression. The sentient being that was the object of the mind trick tended to adopt a casual tone of voice but a peculiar facial expression. Should the trick succeed, he or she then agreed to whatever was being said to them without being able to think for themselves. Moments later, they would feel puzzled about their new opinion, but usually didn't feel like changing it back.

Experienced Force users could Force persuade over long distances&mdash;in one instance, between starships.<ref name="Star Wars 1998 5">In [[Star Wars (1998) 5|''Star Wars'' (1998) 5]], Ki-Adi-Mundi Force persuades a Trade Federation ship to allow him to land on Tatooine.</ref>

Usage of the mind trick in the proper manner was a moral precept for the Jedi, as it did violate the individual's free will and conscience. Thus, the Jedi were strictly prohibited from using it for personal gain (such as in betting or bargaining), reserving its use for when it would serve the greater good and encouraged to use other means if possible;<ref name="Essential Guide to the Force" /> though to some Jedi of the New Jedi Order like Master Durron , it was a small matter to bend others’ minds;<ref name="The New Jedi Order: Dark Journey">''[[The New Jedi Order: Dark Journey]]''</ref> the Sith and other Dark Jedi, however, had no qualms about the usage of the ability.

When instructing Jedi students, Yarael Poof stressed that a user must be mindful when utilizing this ability, that their target was nevertheless a living being with a life of their own, and that extra precaution must be exercised as their command could potentially ruin their target's life or even confuse the target into self-harmful actions or make someone become literally sacred to death.<ref name="Essential Guide to the Force" /> Mind tricks could also be used to convert individuals to fight for another.<ref name="TFU II">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II]]''</ref>

This power sometimes required the complete concentration of the user. Worries such as whether or not it would work or allowing one to be distracted by the insight gained into the mind of the subject would cause the trick to fail.<ref name="Shadows of the Empire">[[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (novel)|''Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire'' novel]]</ref>

===Force confusion===
Among the more advanced mind trick techniques was Force confusion, which could be used in combat to temporarily manipulate enemies to fight as an ally. It was especially useful when outnumbered, and was quicker to employ than affect mind in the heat of battle.

===Force fear===
[[File:Force_Fear_TotC.jpg|thumb|right|200px|right|A darksider using Force fear]]
{{Quote|Terror is a cancer, devouring the mind from within. Strength, hope, and wisdom are nothing but thoughts to be consumed.|Unidentified darksider|<ref name="TOTC">{{SWGTCG|set=Threat of the Conqueror|cardname=Force Fear}}</ref>}}
Force fear was a [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark-side]] [[The Force/Legends|Force]] [[Force power/Legends|power]] and possibly a dark-side variant on the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] mind trick, used around [[4000 BBY/Legends|4000 BBY]] by [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] and [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Jedi with dark-side tendencies]]. The wielder would strike directly at the deepest parts of the target's mind, causing an uncontrollable shaking fear that would wreak havoc with the target's capabilities. Through pure force of will alone, a user could cause them to lose their courage completely, and if left undefended, the effects could be severe, rapidly demoralizing the enemy with a feeling of hopelessness and regret. Depending on the victim, it would caused them to either cower defenselessly or flee from their opponent. A note to keep in mind is that Force Fear taps into the primordial fears locked in all beings' subconscious and primitive brain

Force Fear was classified as a dark-side power because fear was an emotion of the dark side. However, as with many powers, it was the intent behind its use that counted, and Jedi would sometimes use it to defuse a potential dangerous situation.

Force fear had two advanced variants: Force horror and Force insanity. Force horror enabled the [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force user]] to cause multiple enemies to enter into a catatonic state of panic that was more severe and more difficult to defend than the basic Force fear. In similarity, Force insanity also enabled the Force user to affect multiple enemies at once, although to an even greater range than its predecessor. As the most advanced form of Force fear, its effect was much more devastating, with the victims possibly descending into an utter state of frenzied madness and deranged mania as their situation seemed to suddenly become hopeless.

===Mind control===
Also known as [[Qâzoi Kyantuska|dominate mind or control mind]], mind control was the dark-side equivalent of the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] mind trick, though mind control was much more invasive. It took complete control of the mind(s) of the victim(s) affected by the power.<ref name="Book of Sith" /> Higher levels of mastery allowed more people to be controlled, though its effect on members of certain species with an innate immunity to mind tricks (such as [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]] or [[Toydarian/Legends|Toydarians]]) is unconfirmed.

===Force corrupt===
{{Quote|Wise Jedi have said that the Force can have a strong influence on the weak-minded. In typical Jedi fashion, they understand this truth, but lack the courage to make full use of it.|Unidentified darksider|<ref name="SOC">{{SWGTCG|set=Squadrons Over Corellia|cardname=Force Corruption}}</ref>}}
[[File:Force_Corruption_SOC.png|thumb|left|200px|A Dark Jedi using Force corruption to control a clone shadow trooper]]
One sinister variation of the power was Force Corruption, an ability that would force targets to the user's side, while slowly draining their life.<ref name="EaW">''[[Star Wars: Empire at War]]''</ref>

Force corrupt or Force corruption was a dark-side ability that could temporarily manipulate the minds of other sentient beings and make them serve one's own cause. During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], it was sometimes employed by the Force users of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], possibly including [[Mara Jade Skywalker|Mara Jade]] and Palpatine himself, taking control of enemy soldiers and making them serve the cause of the Empire by attacking other enemy units.

Force corrupt was possibly a dark-side variant of the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] mind trick, wherein the Force user employs similar principles, but to influence the target for violent purposes rather than deceiving them.

===Mind Twist===
This technique was a variation of the mind trick developed by [[Daegen Lok]] where he intruded into another's consciousness and twisted their perception of reality to suit his own ends. Lok's skill with the ability was such that he was able to convince [[Tau (individual)|Xesh]] that he was suffocating, and he convinced [[Bel Zana]]'s mind that she was on fire to the point where her body exhibited burn marks.

===Force illusion===
{{Quote|There's no telling what kind of illusions a Jedi Knight can create with the Force.|[[Natasi Daala]]|<ref name="Fate of the Jedi: Vortex">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Vortex]]''</ref>}}
[[File:AleemaKetoSithIllusion-DLotS4.jpg|thumb|right|300px|[[Aleema Keto]] demonstrates her proficiency in creating illusions.]]
Force illusion was a very powerful Force ability, a subset of the various mind trick powers. The [[Force-sensitive/Legends|user]] projected an image into the minds of beings within range, of anything from a pillar of fire to a horde of snarling monsters to a fleet of warships, depending on the range. The user could "see" the illusion as well, though it would be only partially there, semi-transparent like a hologram.

The key differences between a [[The Force/Legends|Force]] illusion and a hologram is that unlike a hologram, the illusion could be controlled mentally and was limited only by the imagination of the user. Even more importantly, a Force illusion did not merely affect the sight of a creature. Since it was projected directly into the brain of the creature, it appeared on all of the creature's senses, from hearing to smell to senses such as echolocation. Even viewing it through an electronic system such as a cybernetic eye or camera was of no use if the creature was within range of the illusion during its duration; the creature would "see" it with the system as if the illusion were actually there, though any playback after the illusion had ended would reveal nothing at all.

Though powerful, it was not without its drawbacks. It had a greatly reduced (or almost nonexistent) effect on Force users or Force-resistant [[Species/Legends|species]] such as [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]] and [[Yuuzhan Vong]]. It was also difficult to learn. While Force illusions could make something out of nothing, they couldn't make nothing out of something (in other words, render someone invisible; for that aspect, [[Force immersion]] would be used), though they could conceal anything within the illusion. In addition, the illusion offered no physical substance. Though it could be "felt," in most cases, any appendage that touched it would pass straight through, usually betraying its status. Finally, the sustained use of a Force illusion could be taxing, especially at the extreme ranges of the skill (thousands of kilometers, large enough to affect [[Capital ship/Legends|capital-ship]] combat).

[[Lumiya]] used Force illusion on mirrors in her bedroom, to make the reflected people look more attractive than they really were. The [[Fallanassi/Legends|Fallanassi]], due to their abilities to manipulate the [[White Current/Legends|White Current]], were capable of creating powerful illusions. However, unlike most Force-sensitives, illusions created through the White Current could be created to be as insubstantial or as real as the user wanted, with the most convincing illusions being indistinguishable visually from a real object. Conversely, [[Fallanassi/Legends|Fallanassi]] illusions could be intentionally insubstantial, so as to trick a sentient into thinking that something that was real wasn't real.<ref name="CTD">''[[Cracken's Threat Dossier]]''</ref>

[[File:Force_Illusion_IE.png|thumb|left|250px|A Mirialan Force-user casts an illusion to escape pursuit]]
Yarael Poof, being described as a "consummate illusionist," was an adept at Force illusions, and was known to have used them on various occasions. Through the Force, Poof would determine an opponent's innate fears. Based on these fears, he would project images of them to wholesale armies, prompting quick, deliberate ends to battles that would otherwise have erupted into bloodshed. In some ways, this was not unlike the effects of Force fear, albeit a different method.<ref name="Essential Guide to the Force" />

A known variant of Force illusion was masquerade. Masquerade enabled the user to project an image into a person's mind over the user, essentially masking the user's appearance.

The dark-side technique for creating illusions, or mindforms, involved conjuring visible, lifelike astral projections of whatever the conjurer desired through the use of [[Sith sorcery/Legends|Sith sorcery]]. The illusions distorted all of an individual's sensory perceptions, and only through concentration on the Force was an individual able to perceive them as being false.

By simply gesturing with one's hands, a [[Sith sorcerer]] could create whatever manifestations they desired. As an application of the dark side, Sith sorcerers tended to create hideous forms of serpents and other creatures to torment victims.<ref name="darklords1">[[Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith 1|''Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith'' 1]]</ref> Playing on all the victim's senses, the illusion could seemingly attack individuals, should they actually believe the apparition to be real. However, the illusion could be undone should the victim cease to believe it exists. The illusions could also be undone if the conjuring sorcerer is interrupted by a powerful [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light side]] attack.<ref name="darklords2">[[Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith 2|''Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith'' 2]]</ref>

The ancient [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Naga Sadow/Legends|Naga Sadow]] was a master of illusion casting. His possessed considerable natural ability, but to augment the strength of his illusions Sadow would often employ the use of [[Sith talisman/Legends|Sith amulets]] or technology. During the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]], he would sit in [[Naga Sadow's Mothership|his meditation sphere]] and project magnificent illusions of war beasts on the battlefields of [[Empress Teta/Legends|Koros Major]], [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] and [[Kirrek]]. His concentration was broken, however, when one of his own capital ships fired upon his meditation sphere, causing his magical illusions to fade, eventually leading to Sith defeats on all three planets.<ref name="fall4">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire 4|''Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire'' 4]]</ref>

When the [[Spacer/Legends|spacer]] [[Gav Daragon]] was being initiated as a [[Sith apprentice/Legends|Sith apprentice]] by Sadow, he received from Sadow rudimentary instruction in creating illusions. Daragon's strength was minimal, for every illusion he conjured turned from something pleasing into a hideous spectral form.<ref name="GAOTS4">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith 4|''Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith'' 4]]</ref>

[[File:WyyrlokIllusion.jpg|thumb|right|250px|[[Darth Wyyrlok (III)|Darth Wyyrlok III]] uses illusions to distract the warriors of [[Malevolence (cult)|the Malevolence]].]]
[[Sith sorcerer|Sith sorceress]] [[Aleema Keto]] was rather proficient with this ability. By simply gesturing with her hands, Aleema could create whatever manifestations she desired. Among her more popular creations were hideous forms of serpents and other creatures she used to [[Torture/Legends|torture]] victims, like the [[Adegan eel]] she replaced her former tutor [[Korus]]' tongue with.<ref name="darklords1" /> During the [[Battle of Koros Major]], Aleema envisioned [[space grazer]]s and massive [[Warship/Legends|warships]] against the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] [[Republic Navy/Legends|fleet]].<ref name="darklords2" /> She could also form more obscure illusions, like turning swords into living animals, technology into monsters, or phantoms of severed heads.<ref name="darklords1" />

The [[Nightsisters/Legends|Nightsisters]] of [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomir]] had a perception of the Force very different than that of the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] and the Sith, an integral part of which was the casting of illusions through "illusion spells."<ref name="RIE">''[[Star Wars: Infinity's End]]''</ref><ref name="WoDM">''[[The Wrath of Darth Maul]]''</ref><ref name="Restraint">{{StoryCite|story=Restraint|book=Darth Maul: Shadow Hunter}}</ref><ref name="CWM">{{TCW|Massacre}}</ref>

Around [[137 ABY]], [[Darth Wyyrlok (III)|Darth Wyyrlok]] used this spell [[Mission to Prakith (Darth Wyyrlok)|against]] [[Demtri]] and [[Gerlun]], members of [[Malevolence (cult)|the Malevolence]], in [[Andeddu's Keep]] on the planet [[Prakith/Legends|Prakith]], making the cult tear itself apart, for example fooling Gerlun into killing Demtri. [[Darth Andeddu|Lord Andeddu]]--brought back to undead awareness and power by Gerlun sacrificing himself--and Wyyrlok then battled each other with illusions potent enough to inflict real injury on their targets, a contest that Andeddu ultimately lost.<ref name="Leg27">[[Legacy (2006) 27|''Legacy'' (2006) 27]]</ref>

===Force projection===
[[File:Projection.jpg|thumb|left|200px|[[Mara Jade Skywalker|Mara Jade]] (right) and her Force projection]]
Force projection was a mysterious Force ability and was possibly a variation of Force illusion. [[Darth Ramage]], a [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Scientist/Legends|scientist]], extensively researched this technique, recording his findings on his [[Holocron/Legends|holocron]], [[SD41263.I]]. It enabled the user to create and "program" an apparition similar to themselves to distract, confuse or lure enemies. The illusion could be animate<ref name="TLJ">[[The Last Jedi (novel)|''The Last Jedi'']]</ref> or inanimate, was fully capable of intercepting incoming fire and was visible to all around it, not just a selected target. A similar ability that was primarily associated to the dark side was [[Force phantom]], which required [[Sith sorcery/Legends|Sith rituals]] to tether the illusion created by the castor to a living creature, which would die if the illusion were destroyed.

==Users==
{{Quote|You weak-minded fool! He's using an old Jedi mind trick!|translated=1|Jabba Desilijic Tiure to Bib Fortuna|<ref name="Episode 6" />}}
[[3964 BBY|Almost four thousand years]] before the Battle of Yavin, on [[Taris/Legends|Taris]], [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Zayne Carrick]] tried to use a mind trick on [[Marn Hierogryph]] but he complained that such tricks were useless on him. In [[3956 BBY]], during his quest for the Star Forge, Revan may have used this ability many times, though he was warned by [[Bastila Shan]] against using it for personal gains, such as bargaining for low prices. A [[3951 BBY|few years]] later, [[Meetra Surik]], known as The Exile, and [[Kreia]] used the mind trick to make people forget that they were even there. In addition, the Exile also used the technique much in the way that Revan had previously. More than [[3640 BBY|three hundred years later]], [[Gnost-Dural]] used the mind trick on a [[Nikto/Legends|Nikto]] standing guard in front of the [[Crooked Finger]] bar to avoid paying a demanded cover charge. [[Theron Shan]] expressed that his life would be a lot easier if he could do that and Gnost-Dural noted that it doesn't work on everyone and that Nikto was particularly susceptible.

[[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]] utilized this power prior to the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] attack on [[Theed/Legends|Theed]]. Other practitioners of the ability included [[Tenebrae]], [[Kreia]], [[Joruus C'baoth]], [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], and [[Luuke Skywalker]]. Skillful users could manipulate the thoughts and actions of their targets, as well as their memories, emotions and senses.

[[44 BBY/Legends|Twelve years]] prior to the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], while aboard the freighter [[Monument (freighter)|''Monument'']], [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] attempted to persuade [[Jemba]] the Hutt to return their [[dactyl]] to the [[Arcona/Legends|Arcona]] workers in the [[Arcona Mineral Harvest Corporation]]. Unfortunately, he had been focusing so much on healing his recent wound from a fight with a [[Togorian/Legends|Togorian]] [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]] and was too weak to change Jemba's mind. Later, on [[Bandomeer/Legends|Bandomeer]], Jinn used a mind trick on a Hutt guard working for the [[Offworld Mining Corporation]] to grant him access to the [[Xanatos's private office|private office]] of his former [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]], [[Xanatos]]. In [[33 BBY/Legends|33 BBY]], while in a [[Cantina/Legends|cantina]] on [[Dorvalla/Legends|Dorvalla]], Darth Maul used a mind trick on a bartender so that she would "bring him his drink and leave him alone." A [[32 BBY/Legends|year later]], while on [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]], Qui-Gon Jinn used a mind trick to convince the leader of the [[Gungan/Legends|Gungans]], [[Rugor Nass/Legends|Boss Nass]], to allow Jinn and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] to depart in a [[Tribubble bongo/Legends|bongo]] with [[Jar Jar Binks/Legends|Jar Jar Binks]]. Shortly thereafter, on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], Jinn attempted to convince [[Watto/Legends|Watto]], a [[Toydarian/Legends|Toydarian]] junk dealer, to allow him to use [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|Republic credits]] to buy spare parts for Queen [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Amidala's]] royal starship. Watto asked Jinn if he thought he was "some kind of Jedi, waving [his] hand around like that." Watto claimed that mind tricks did not work on his species. During this same time, Qui-Gon used the mind trick to convince a pushy [[Sebulba/Legends|Sebulba]] to wait outside while he talked with Watto after the [[Boonta Eve Classic (32 BBY)/Legends|Boonta Eve Race]] and later to make a cruel slave owner give his [[Slavery/Legends|slaves]] [[Water/Legends|water]] and to never harm them again.<ref name="Star Wars: Episode I Adventures">''[[Star Wars: Episode I Adventures]]''</ref>

The [[Quermian/Legends|Quermian]] [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Yarael Poof/Legends|Yarael Poof]] was one of the most famous users of mind tricks before his [[Death/Legends|death]] in [[27 BBY/Legends|27 BBY]].<ref name="Essential Guide to the Force" />

[[File:Force_Illusion_JATM.png|thumb|right|265x265px|A Jedi General projects an illusion of additional starships during the Clone Wars.]]
[[22 BBY/Legends|A decade later]], on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], Obi-Wan Kenobi refused the offer of a [[Slythmonger/Legends|slythmonger]], [[Elan Sel'Sabagno/Legends|Elan Sel'Sabagno]], for cilona-extract "[[Death stick/Legends|death sticks]]," which were powerful narcotics. Kenobi convinced the slythmonger with a wave of his hand that he didn't want to sell him death sticks, and instead he wanted to "go home and rethink his life." A few days later, while hiding on Naboo, [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]] asked [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] if he was going to use the mind trick on her. He replied that it would only work on the weak-minded, implying that Padmé's mind was too strong&mdash;and Anakin knew it.

[[22 BBY/Legends|Early in]] the Clone Wars, [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]] used the mind trick to make Captain [[Gregar Typho/Legends|Typho]]&mdash;responsible for Padmé Amidala's safety&mdash;recommend that they needed to save [[Luminara Unduli/Legends|Luminara Unduli]] and [[Barriss Offee/Legends|Barriss Offee]] on [[Ilum/Legends|Ilum]], which was a "slight deviation" from their route. Although Padmé clearly recognized the trick, she still happily ordered Typho to go to Ilum. In [[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]], [[Asajj Ventress/Legends|Asajj Ventress]] used a mind trick on [[Clone Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Rex/Legends|Rex]] to force him to contact Anakin Skywalker. Rex managed to resist the trick and instead covertly warned Skywalker of the danger. Later that year, while in captivity to the pirate [[Hondo Ohnaka/Legends|Hondo Ohnaka]], Obi-Wan Kenobi used a mind trick on a [[Weequay/Legends|Weequay]] pirate to convince him that he did not want to stand guard, but instead wanted to deactivate the cell bars and go out drinking. [[Duros/Legends|Duros]] bounty hunter [[Cad Bane/Legends|Cad Bane]] was coerced to reveal the location of the [[Kyber memory crystal/Legends|kyber memory crystal]] and two [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] children. Bane was resistant at first, but the combined power of [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]] overwhelmed the bounty hunter's mental defenses, forcing him to reluctantly revealed the location of the memory crystal and children. Also in 21 BBY, [[Ahsoka Tano/Legends|Ahsoka Tano]] used a Jedi mind trick twice on a [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidian]] guard on a [[Lucrehulk-class battleship/Legends|Trade Federation Battleship]] to allow her and Senator [[Riyo Chuchi/Legends|Riyo Chuchi]] into the detention block to rescue [[Chi Eekway Papanoida/Legends|Chi Eekway Papanoida]]. While being hunted for sport on the moon of [[Wasskah/Legends|Wasskah]], [[Jedi Initiate/Legends|Jedi Initiate]] [[Jinx/Legends|Jinx]] tried using a mind trick on [[Trandoshan/Legends|Trandoshan]] hunter [[Smug/Legends|Smug]] to call a speeder, but it didn't work the first time. After [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] hit the Trandoshan on the head, [[Smug/Legends|Smug]] became susceptible to Jedi mind tricks, and ended up calling a speeder which then was hijacked by [[O-Mer/Legends|O-Mer]].

Just before the conclusion of the war, Obi-Wan Kenobi again used a mind trick to avoid any unnecessary entanglements on the sinkhole world of [[Utapau/Legends|Utapau]]. In order to procure transport needed to track down [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]], Kenobi used the Force to persuade a local [[Utai/Legends|Utai]] dragonmount-handler to assist him. The Utai allowed Kenobi to ride [[Boga/Legends|Boga]], a loyal [[Varactyl/Legends|varactyl]] mount, to reach the [[tenth level]] of [[Pau City/Legends|Pau City]] where he located Grievous and eventually killed him. After the execution of [[Order 66/Legends|Order 66]], when Kenobi returned to [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] along with Senator [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Organa]] and Master [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]], they were greeted by a guard; the guard said that he would take the Jedi into his custody, but Kenobi employed a mind trick persuading the guard that it would be better if the Jedi remained with the Senator.

In [[3 BBY/Legends|3 BBY]], [[Galen Marek|Starkiller]] used the mind trick several times during the course of his mission for [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]]. He used it to interrogate a [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]] bartender as to the whereabouts of [[Rahm Kota/Legends|Rahm Kota]], forced an Imperial officer on [[Felucia/Legends|Felucia]] to reveal the location of Senator Bail Organa, and attempted to persuade [[Lobot/Legends|Lobot]] to grant him an audience with Senator [[Garm Bel Iblis/Legends|Garm Bel Iblis]]; however, because Lobot's brain was [[Borg Construct Aj^6|cybernetically enhanced]], the mind trick had no effect on him.

[[1 BBY/Legends|Two years later]], after the beginning of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], [[Subject 1138|Galen Marek's clone]] used mind tricks to make Imperials turn on their allies or commit suicide on numerous occasions.<ref name="TFU II" /> [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] twisted the wills of Imperial units such as [[Strike force Alpha]] to the dark side so that if a Jedi tried to convert a unit, they would commit suicide.<ref name="SW:GB">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]''</ref>

[[File:Mindtrick2.png|thumb|left|250px|Luke Skywalker used a mind trick on Bib Fortuna after entering Jabba's Palace.]]
In [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]] Kenobi once more made use of the Jedi mind trick, this time to convince a stormtrooper that [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] and he did not have the [[Droid/Legends|droids]] for which the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Empire]] was searching and that it would be best if they were allowed to move along. Pilot [[BoShek/Legends|BoShek]] used latent Force ability, along with residual effects from Kenobi's trick, to perform a mind trick which allowed him to escape from four stormtroopers after "borrowing" a [[Landspeeder/Legends|landspeeder]]. Weeks later, [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] used a mind trick to force [[Bib Fortuna/Legends|Bib Fortuna]] and a group of guards to let them go after a bounty hunter took [[Grubba Desilijic Aarrpo|Grubba]] from them.

In [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], Luke Skywalker entered [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|Jabba's Palace]] to rescue [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]]. He used the mind trick to convince Bib Fortuna to grant him an audience with [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba the Hutt]]. Jabba later criticized Fortuna for falling for such a "old mind trick" and after Skywalker tried to use it on the Hutt, told the Jedi that his mind powers would not work on him.

After the death of Emperor [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], [[Corran Horn/Legends|Corran Horn]] unknowingly used the mind trick to hide from stormtroopers during his escape from the ''[[Lusankya/Legends|Lusankya]]'' in [[6 ABY/Legends|6 ABY]]. The [[7 ABY/Legends|following year]], Horn tried to intentionally use a mind trick on a stormtrooper while on an undercover mission on [[Thyferra/Legends|Thyferra]]. For a moment, when the stormtrooper repeated Horn's statement about not having to go with him, Horn thought the trick was actually working. It failed miserably, and the only reaction he prompted from the stormtrooper was "You can go about your business? Your business is my business, void brain!" Horn was injured by the stormtrooper and ended up having to spend a couple of days in a [[Bacta tank/Legends|bacta tank]] to recover. After [[11 ABY/Legends|having begun]] studies to become a Jedi, Horn successfully projected an illusion of a huge [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] task force, complete with ''[[Lusankya/Legends|Lusankya]]'' and [[Sun Crusher]], into the brain of [[Leonia Tavira]]'s, leader of the [[Invids]].

[[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] used this power on the animal denizens of lower Coruscant to protect himself and his companions during the Corellian crisis. He opted to jolt the animals' minds with fear as he was faced with a large pack and fear was the most readily recognizable emotion available. He did this to preserve everyone's life.

The [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] [[Yuuzhan Vong]] [[Onimi]] evidently used mind control on [[Supreme Overlord]] [[Shimrra Jamaane]] during their reign over the species, but towards the end of the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], Onimi lost control of Shimrra. He later attributed this, as he claims to [[Jaina Solo Fel|Jaina Solo]], to his "preoccupation with defeating you [Jaina] allowed what remained of Shimrra to reemerge"; this is implied that he was somehow distracted in his greater battle with [[Yun'o]], which caused this loss of control over Shimrra.

In [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]], during the [[Second Galactic Civil War]], [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa Solo]] used a mind trick on a lieutenant from the [[Second Fleet (Galactic Alliance)|Galactic Alliance Second Fleet]] vessel ''[[Spinnerfish]]''. She tricked him first into believing that [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]] (who was using the identity [[Bescat Offdurmin]] at the time) was not offering aid and comfort to the enemy, then that they had to get to [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]] because they were doing something vital to the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Alliance]] and finally to give them the access codes provided by [[Galactic Alliance Fleet Intelligence|Intelligence]] that would allow them to fly in directly. Afterward, Lando commented "That wasn't really fair" and Leia responded that the lieutenant was "even more weak-minded" than she was used to and she didn't think he'd progress far in the army. [[Ben Skywalker]] used a mind trick on [[Gilthor Breen]] to persuade him that he had entered a turbolift. He projected an image of the turbolift doors closing and directed him to think about "the girl," a holodrama actress named [[Aliniaca Verr]]. Notably, Ben accomplished this trick without the use of either a hand gesture or his voice. [[Mara Jade Skywalker|Mara Jade]] used a mind trick on two bystanders after fighting with [[Lumiya]]. She tricked the two bystanders into believing that the battle that they just witnessed between Mara and Lumiya was staged for a hol- program. The male bystander remarked that the blood on Mara's face looked real, tricked by Mara into believing that it was fake. In 41 ABY, during the [[Second Battle of Fondor]], [[Darth Caedus]] used the Force to mind trick the Fondorians into lowering the planetary shield based around the city of Oridin, opening the city to bombardment by his forces.

In [[137 ABY]], Princess [[Marasiah Fel]] attempted to use a mind trick on [[Cade Skywalker]] in order to get aboard the [[Mynock (Helot-class)|''Mynock'']] with [[Astraal Vao]] and away from [[Darth Talon]]. Cade (a former Jedi) was not affected, but took them anyway after spotting the Sith. Cade later said to his companions, "Human thinks I'm some weak willed Koochu&mdash;tried a Jedi 'mind trick.'"

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|I'm amazed at how many people that works on. Is the whole galaxy made up of weak-minded fools?|[[Canderous Ordo]] in response to Revan using a mind trick|<ref name="KOTOR1" />}}
Various games represent the Jedi mind trick as a means of slipping past opponents without being seen. In one instance it was named "Force persuasion," but accomplished the same thing, probably a name to apply only to this variant of use. A mind trick in the game is employed, and the character becomes invisible to (an) opponent(s). Some games allow players to use the mind trick to confuse and stun their opponents; others employ the mind trick to cause opponents to temporarily switch allegiance by attacking other opponents.

The mind trick is known as both '''affect mind''' and the more powerful '''dominate mind''' in ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''. In ''Knights of the Old Republic'' and its sequel, [[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords|''Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords'']], usage of mind-affecting Force abilities follows the movies more closely. Learning these abilities gives the player additional choices in conversations, which can be used to persuade NPCs to do something beneficial for the player&mdash;for example, pay a greater reward than the player would normally receive, offer a lower price for an item, share some secret information, extract information from the individual, or manipulate them into doing or accepting various things.

In the comic version of [[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith|''Dark Lords of the Sith'']], Aleema's cousin Satal Keto never displays a proficiency with illusion casting. However, in the [[Tales of the Jedi: Dark Lords of the Sith (audio drama)|''Dark Lords of the Sith audio rendition'']], Satal creates illusions and uses them to confound his father and aunt, [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] [[Keto]] and Lady [[Magda Keto]].<ref name="DLOTSA" />

In [[Star Wars: Jedi Knight II: Jedi Outcast|''Jedi Knight II: Jedi Outcast'']] and [[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy|''Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy'']], if the player character has a mind trick level higher than 3 (impossible without cheats), he may directly control an enemy including [[Reborn]], which are normally immune to the ability. On level 4, this power could affect anyone, even on the strongest minds like [[Desann]] or [[Tavion Axmis]].

Force confusion is a usable power in ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''. It is available if the [[Meetra Surik|Jedi Exile]] attains a prestige class. Game files from ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]'' indicate [[Jolee Bindo]] was meant to have the psychic static ability. Whether it was cut by choice or due to time constraints is unknown.

Force confusion is also present in the [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith (video game)|Star Wars Episode III video game]].

In ''[[I, Jedi]]'', [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] refers to both his and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi's]] use of mind control as Alter Mind.
